about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

survivors.reason: first byte of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA's VALUE image is CDEMO-FROM-TRANID(1:1); MAIN-PARA's MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) TO CARDDEMO-COMMAREA overwrites all of it when EIBCALEN > 0, and with EIBCALEN = 0 RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN's MOVE WS-TRANID TO CDEMO-FROM-TRANID does, before the XCTL sends it

IMAGE of DFHCOMMAREA (a later chunk): COUSR02C reads DFHCOMMAREA only as DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN), at most the 194 bytes of its COMMAREA, which in_ writes from the caller's COMMAREA first; this byte of the 32767-byte image lies past them, and for a terminal task the area's final contents are not observable (CICS discards them; linked_result drops them)

the base offset of fill_ for the task's COMMAREA object: for a terminal task (level 1) the COMMAREA object is not observable (CICS discards it; linked_result drops it), and the RETURN / XCTL COMMAREA is built by out_ from CARDDEMO-COMMAREA

the byte[] COMMAREA entry (`ca instanceof byte[]`) runs only for a LINK from a Java caller handing raw bytes; no CardDemo program LINKs this program (no EXEC CICS LINK exists in the app; it is a terminal program reached by XCTL), so the area is always the typed DTO

survivors.before: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length - keep); } };
survivors.after: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond == null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length - keep); } };
survivors.reason: the raw-area write-back runs only for a task entered with a LINK area (`task.linkArea()` non-null); the case enters by a terminal transaction

cutting DFHCOMMAREA to EIBCALEN bytes (X23) matters only to a reference past EIBCALEN; COUSR02C reads DFHCOMMAREA only as DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN), the plumbing's own in_ runs before the cut and fill_ after caWhole restores the whole array, and at calen == the area's length the cut keeps every byte, so cutting or not is unobservable

the 'Y' written when the REWRITE fails is never tested afterwards: UPDATE-USER-INFO's ERR-FLG tests ran before it, and MAIN-PARA's PF3 / PF5 paths go on to the XCTL or the RETURN without testing it; the next task starts from initialState's 'N'

`CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM = LOW-VALUES AND = SPACES` for OR: every caller of RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN moves a program name into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM first ('COSGN00C', CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM when it is not blank, else 'COADM01C'), so it is neither, and both conditions are false
the `return 4` falls through to the next paragraph after an XCTL that answered something but NORMAL; COUSR02C has no HANDLE and no RESP on it, so condition() abends first
COUSR02C never reads EIBRESP2, so its value cannot show

condition() returns a value only for a handled, ignored or ERROR-handled condition; COUSR02C sets no handler and an XCTL raises none ignored by default, so condition() throws (the abend) and `to` is never tested
